sourceNote: reference/<sha>/src/index.html is film-engine's src/index.html at sourceCommit, so this repo checks itself without ../film-engine. To resync: bump sourceCommit, `git -C ../film-engine show <sha>:src/index.html > reference/<short>/src/index.html`, re-copy backend/ at the same sha, npm run split, npm test.

backendLocalChanges.backend/lib/music-approval.js: SCORE_CONSUMERS: playback's code is the React page's engine, src/pages/playback/player.js, not src/index.html
backendLocalChanges.backend/lib/graph-hold.js: pgRunPending is in the Production graph page's engine, src/pages/productiongraph/engine.js, not src/index.html
backendLocalChanges.backend/lib/framing.js: comment: SHOT_FRAMINGS now lives in public/legacy/chunks/stage3d.js
backendLocalChanges.backend/lib/previs-subject-path.js: comment: subjectPoseAt's mirror now lives in public/legacy/chunks/stage3d.js
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/REMOVED-TESTS.txt: v2 only: the film-engine tests this copy does not carry, each with its reason
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/SKIPPED-SUBTESTS.json: v2 only: sub-tests skipped by exact name, each with its reason
backendLocalChanges.backend/routes/shots.js: getShotlist answers every shot unless limit/page is given: the default of 50 cut a film past 50 shots out of every page that lists shots (Shot Board, scene dialogue, subtitles picker, export, previs, score session)
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/shotlist-all.test.js: v2 only: holds the shot list to answering every shot unless paged
backendLocalChanges.backend/server.js: routes shot-audit and shots-resync to handleProductionReports: the handler served them but server.js never routed them, so they answered 405 (Resync, the MCP shots_resync tool, Sync screenplay); held by backend/tests/report-routes-reachable.test.js
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/report-routes-reachable.te: v2 only: every report production-reports.js serves is routed to it by server.js
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/budget-backend-halves.test: v2 only: the backend halves of two sub-tests whose last line reads the legacy Budget page (production-estimate's route and tool, requested-size's per-model maximum), kept verbatim
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/page-handlers.test.js: ownScript reads a React page's own code from its <template data-react-source> (tools/assemble-page.js), taking the templates out before the script scan (an engine's regex can hold `<script`): engines define the functions the page's controls and HTML call
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/flow-canvas-reach.test.js: the graph renderers that name a flow are read from the Production graph page's engine template (assemble-page), not after `let PRODUCTION_GRAPH_ON`, which stayed in core; its fake browser gives loadFlowsPage legacy.PRODUCTION_GRAPH_ON: the Flows engine reads core's flag through the bridge
v2 only: the parts of three screenplay sub-tests that still read correctly from the page source (the originals are skipped; the button reads are held in src/pages/screenplay)
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/page-parses.test.js: every inline script compiles: React page source templates (<template data-react-source>) are inert text, not scripts, and are left out
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/previs-routes.test.js: the SPA script parses: React page source templates are inert text, not scripts, and are left out
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/audio-cards.test.js: the sandbox that runs soundCueCard gives it legacy.API_BASE: the music engine reads core's API_BASE through the bridge
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/previs-board-view.test.js: the sandbox that runs the console's frame functions gives them legacy.API_BASE: the 3D stage engine reads core's API_BASE through the bridge
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/shot-motion.test.js: the sandbox that runs previsAim gives it legacy.P_DEG: the 3D stage engine reads core's P_DEG through the bridge
backendLocalChanges.backend/tests/console-regions.test.js: the console's source is read up to the end of its <template> (the 3D stage engine's source block), not to the end of the page, where other components' text follows
a loading renderer's body is bounded by its own braces, not by the next top-level function: as core's declarations move into React engines, "the next function" can be far away and the slice ran into unrelated code

pinToCore.twBurst: stays next to const TYPEWRITER (core): screenplay-focus reads the typewriter's sound rules as the source text from TYPEWRITER to twBurst, which must be one script
